Patient is a 34 yo teacher with episodic wheeze since childhood, worse in spring and with cold air, and she notes that symptoms flare when the classroom is cleaned with a particular spray. She had two courses of oral steroids last year, uses her rescue inhaler about three times a week, and wakes at night roughly once a week. Her mother and brother have hay fever, she has a cat at home, and she is planning to move to a new apartment in the fall that she hopes will have fewer carpets. She jogs on weekends but stops at about two miles because of chest tightness. PFT: obstruction, reversible.
Normal pulmonary function study.
